extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for evaluating large multimodal models on joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images across eight real-world scenarios.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan; Hritik Bansal; Kai-Wei Chang; Nanyun Peng
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 235, 2024)
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, Rohan; Bansal, Hritik; Chang, Kai-Wei; Peng, Nanyun. CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected following guidelines that each sample be an <image, instruction, response> triplet requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements, avoiding instructions solvable by OCR/text alone, covering both questions and imperative tasks, and varying complexity. Images were sourced from six sources and then shortlisted through manual filtering for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories, and heuristic OCR-based filtering for Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes. Annotation proceeded in three stages: image shortlisting, author annotation in two groups across categories, and verification by MTurk workers followed by cross-review by author groups.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from LAION-5B for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories using keyword search with CLIP-retrieval UI; from the Rico Dataset for Application Usage; from website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative with collected screenshots for Web Usage; and from test sets of InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA, which were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs for Infographic and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Existing VQA dataset images from InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA were reannotated with novel instruction-response pairs. For some categories, PaddleOCR was used to detect text and the top 500 images with the highest number of words were selected as candidates, a subset of which was annotated. Incorrect samples identified during verification were filtered out, and author groups reviewed each other's samples to ensure adherence to guidelines and remove low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images in Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories underwent manual filtering to guarantee suitability for annotation. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic-based filtering was performed using PaddleOCR to detect text, after which the top 500 images with the highest number of words were selected and a subset annotated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each instance contains a human-written instruction and a human-written ground-truth response. In Stage 2, the authors were divided into two groups, each responsible for annotating four categories while strictly following annotation guidelines. In Stage 3, MTurk workers verified the correctness of each annotated <image, instruction, response> sample, finding 96% of samples annotated correctly. After filtering incorrect samples, each author group reviewed samples created by the other group.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification by MTurk workers found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and the two author groups reviewed each other's samples to ensure adherence to guidelines and filter low-quality samples. For human evaluation of model responses, three human annotators independently judged each response and majority vote was used as the final decision.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 for human evaluation of predicted responses; 1 verification judgment per sample is not explicitly stated beyond MTurk workers verifying each sample
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human annotators were mainly from the US. MTurk workers used for sample verification were mutually exclusive from those used for the human performance baseline and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code, and a continuously updated leaderboard are made available on the project page. The release plan states that a subset of 100 samples from the 506 will be released as a validation set with reference responses, while reference responses for the remaining 406 samples are kept hidden. The validation set is selected to mirror the overall dataset distribution.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator geography/region (mainly from the US); linguistic diversity and writing style of annotators are discussed as varying across social groups.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is proposed to evaluate context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models for a domain with significant real-world applications, such as assisting the visually impaired and understanding text-rich scenes. The authors state they aimed to ensure images, instructions, and responses are not offensive to any social group. They note that existing multimodal models can generate harmful responses despite safeguards, though they did not observe apparent harmful or privacy-sensitive information in model responses. They also note future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions for more reliable human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that human annotators were mainly from the US, and that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups. They state that future work should involve annotators from more diverse regions. They also note model biases toward prior visual knowledge and hallucinations in qualitative analysis.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for modern LMMs and requires precise visual perception beyond OCR. The authors note MTurk workers found the annotation task time-consuming, making annotation hard within a limited budget. Human evaluation is expensive and hard to scale. Qualitative analysis reveals model failures due to lack of precise visual perception, hallucinations, and limited capacity for fine-grained perception. The authors also note that linguistic diversity and writing style of annotators may vary across social groups, affecting human baseline and evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced as a benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. It is used in the paper for zero-shot and few-shot evaluation, human baseline collection, human evaluation, automatic evaluation, and fine-grained analysis across visual contexts. A subset of 100 samples is planned as a validation set with reference responses, while the remaining 406 samples have hidden references.
